messages.author: 0ad13bc9f91bed5f
messages.subject: New error: "Error in compiler::cmpfun..."
parts:
Hi Nick and everyone else,

I have completed a LOT of BGB runs, but not for about a year. When I get BGB all loaded and ready to go:

"library(BioGeoBEARS)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/cladoRcpp.R") # (needed now that traits model added; source FIRST!)....etc. etc."

I keep getting this error:


> calc_loglike_sp = compiler::cmpfun(calc_loglike_sp_prebyte)    # crucial to fix bug in uppass calculations
> calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch = compiler::cmpfun(calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte)
Error in compiler::cmpfun(calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte) :
  object 'calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte' not found
> # slight speedup hopefully

This happens after I load everything as per the sample script on the BGB phylowiki, if I run old scripts, if I run slight updates/complete updates on the old scripts. I really can't see where I am going wrong!

Can you help - please?

Thank you so much,
Chandra

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] New error: "Error in compiler::cmpfun..."
parts:
Hi-

cladoRcpp and rexpokit have been updated at CRAN, and BioGeoBEARS has been updated at GitHub.

So, these updates should be installed, and then all source() and compiler::cmpfun() commands should be deleted or commented out from old scripts.

See the recent messages on the BioGeoBEARS google group for further hints and help on the updates.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.author: 0ad13bc9f91bed5f
messages.subject: Re: New error: "Error in compiler::cmpfun..."
parts:
Hey Nick (and everyone),

Yes - so I did need to update just about everything(!), my analyses then actually worked/are working. Thanks for the tip! One thing I did note - and it is likely not helpful to many of the 'R' pros who use BGB, but when I loaded the most recent version of BGB - GitHub as suggested, I also needed to load the package 'roxygen2' ie. install.packages ('roxygen2')

I'm not sure why the package could not be found, or loaded without me doing this.

Anyways, until next time :-) Thanks!
Chandra
